senses.gloss: f.(b. h.; preced. wds.) [rootless,] sterile, impotent, barren.
units: <cite ref="Bekhorot 44b:6">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 7:14">Deut. VII, 14</cite>) [read:] <he>לא יהיה בך ע׳ שלא יהיה ביתך ע׳ מן התלמידים</he> ‘there shall be no barren one among thee’, means that thy house shall never be barren of scholars (v.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 848:6">Yalk. Deut. 848</cite>); <cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 3:6">Deut. R. s. 3</cite> <he>עקר ועקרה מן התשובה</he> impotent to give a proper answer (to heretics).
<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 3:17">Ib.</cite> <he>לא תהא תפלתך ע׳</he>, v. <cite ref="P01213"><he>עָקַר</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 53:15">Gen. R. s. 53</cite> <he>לא היית אומר אברם פרדה ע׳ וכ׳</he> didst thou not say, Abram is a barren mule &c.?; <cite ref="Bava Batra 91a:13">B. Bath. 91ᵃ</cite> (in Chald. dict.) <he>כודנא עקרה</he>, v. <cite ref="K00203"><he>כּוּדְנָא</he></cite>; a. fr.—

Num. R. s. 14 (play on עקרת, Num. VII, 55) א״ת קערת אלא עֲקֶרֶת כנגד יעקב וכ׳ read not ḳaʿãrath (dish), but ʿãḳereth (uprooted), corresponding to Jacob who wrested the birthright from Reuben and gave it to Joseph.—Pl. עֲקָרִים; f. עֲקָרוֹת.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 39:16">Gen. R. s. 39</cite> <he>אברהם</he> … <he>על הע׳ וכ׳</he> Abraham prayed for the childless women, and they were visited.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 53:15">Gen. R. s. 53</cite> <he>הרבה ע׳ נפקדו עמה</he> many childless ones were visited at the same time with her (Sarah); a. fr.
